newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes slide late after huge API crude build.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes slide late after huge API crude build.

text.p: U.S. crude prices slipped late Tuesday after the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed a hefty 10.4 million barrel build in crude oil stocks.
The rise was in spite of higher refinery runs, which rose 0.8 pecent to 93.8 percent capacity for the August 23 week.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing fell to $21.30-40 a barrel, down 20 cents from Monday, and off earlier highs on news suggesting some delay in implementing Iraq oil sales.
A top Iraqi U.N. official said on Tuesday the U.S. was hindering the May 20 oil-for-food plan by insisting on too many monitors to supervise the plan.
Domestic grades were traded at mostly steady to firmer levels over the session, with October demand seen picking up.
Light, sweets were resilient with WTI/Midland traded from plus 4-7 cents, up four cents from Monday, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James dealt at 29-30 cents, a few cents higher.
Sours, despite meeting with Latin American competition, managed to stay at recently firmer levels.
West Texas Sour/Midland climbed from minus $1.32 to $1.25 a barrel, up about 10 cents from Monday.
Eugene Island rose to minus $1.20, up 40 cents from Friday, with Bonito done at minus 70 cents, up five cents.
Concerns about disruptions to shipping from Hurricane Edouard, packing winds of 130 miles per hour and potentially a threat to the U.S. East Coast, provided moderate support.
